challenges.title: Why Your Voice Shakes
challenges.challenge: Right now, before your next moment of speaking — class, call, conversation — feel the nerves. Don't push them down. Say out loud: "I'm excited." Then speak immediately. Don't wait for the feeling to change. The excitement label comes first, the feeling follows. Do this once today. Notice that speaking while "excited" feels different than speaking while "nervous," even though your body is doing the exact same thing.

challenges.title: The First 10 Seconds

Or did you warm up first? Now rerecord it: first sentence should be your strongest point, the thing that makes someone want to hear the rest. No introduction, no setup. Just the hook. Compare the two. That's the difference between being ignored and being heard.

challenges.title: Filler Words and Why They Kill You
